name: Confluent and Reticulated Papillomatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Davis et al. Diagnostic Criteria for CRP

criteria.description: Presence of hyperpigmented, scaly, confluent papules forming reticulated plaques primarily on the trunk
No clinical improvement with antifungal therapy
Marked clinical improvement with minocycline treatment
Histopathologic findings showing papillomatosis and hyperkeratosis without fungal elements

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic clinical presentation, lack of response to antifungals, and response to minocycline
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; biopsy and treatment response support diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyperpigmented confluent papules forming reticulated plaques

common.symptomName: Lesions predominantly on upper trunk and neck

occasional.symptomName: Lesions extending to axillae or abdomen

rare.symptomName: Associated mild alopecia over affected areas

laboratory: Negative fungal cultures and KOH prep
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible familial cases reported
other: Histopathology: papillomatosis, hyperkeratosis, acanthosis without fungal elements

distinguishingFeatures: Positive fungal elements on KOH preparation
Lesions often hypopigmented or erythematous rather than hyperpigmented
Velvety thickened plaques primarily in intertriginous areas
Associated with insulin resistance or malignancy

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
references: Davis MD, Weenig RH, et al. Confluent and reticulated papillomatosis: clinical and histopathologic study of 39 cases. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2006.
Fitzpatrick TB. Dermatology in General Medicine. 8th ed. 2012.
James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. 2019.
